title: AB 2047 Becomes Law, the Chube Compact Ships & Metal Printing with Robots
subtitle: This week in 3D printing news

topics.title: AB 2047 Is Law, but It's Asleep
topics.description: Newsom signed California's printer-blocking bill. What it does now, what it could do later, and what we can do about it

slides.heading: AB 2047 Is Law, but It's Asleep
slides.body: Newsom signed it on Saturday, September 26. Nothing changes for anyone today, but my take: this is a big loss for our community.
bullets: Chapter 461, in effect January 1, 2027. Nothing happens until ASTM International writes a blocking-tech standard, and none exists
From July 1, 2027, the CA DOJ checks quarterly. If a standard appears: rules within 24 months, sale ban 1 year later
Earliest possible ban: mid-2028. Realistically 2030 or later

slides.heading: AB 2047: The Off-Ramp and What Got Cut
bullets: No standard by July 1, 2029? The DOJ can stop checking, but the law stays on the books
Cut before signing: criminal penalties, fines, the approved-printer list, a fixed ban date
Also cut: the industrial-printer exemption, which makes the scope wider

slides.heading: What It Means for You
slides.body: Our reading of the text, not legal advice. Once the ban is live, it covers selling a printer, or handing one over in exchange for anything of value.
bullets: Printers you own: untouched. No retrofit, no registration, no limits on use
Giving one away: a true gift isn't covered (friends, family, schools, inheritance). Trades and "free with purchase" probably are
Selling used in CA: covered, with no grandfather clause. Expect lower resale value for California owners
Building your own: parts aren't printers. Kits depend on how the DOJ defines them

slides.heading: What It Means: Builders, Businesses, Everyone Else
bullets: No anti-tampering rule: replacing firmware on your own machine breaks nothing in this law
Businesses: what you print and sell isn't regulated. Fleet purchases and resale in CA are
Outside CA: one global firmware could bring blocking tech to everyone. NY already has a similar law

slides.heading: Brand by Brand: Who Gets Hit How
slides.body: No brand has announced plans. This is my read of how each one is built.
bullets: Bambu: easiest to make comply. Closed, cloud-connected firmware, one global build, so the biggest spillover risk
Prusa: open-source firmware anyone can recompile, so an unremovable lock is close to impossible. Prusa: "way too soon to say"
Sovol & Qidi: Klipper-based and sold heavily on Amazon. Any check would be easy to flash off
VORON: Voron Design sells nothing and parts are outside the law. Exposure: kit vendors, and reselling a build in CA
Prusa and VORON Design both signed the opposition letter

slides.heading: Prop Builders: Our Leverage
slides.body: The law exempts printers used only for film and TV props. That's lawmakers admitting a detector can't tell a prop from a gun.
bullets: 1. ASTM is the on/off switch. Individuals can join its 3D printing committee (F42) and vote on the standard
2. Quote the exemption back: a DL-44 is a Mauser C96 with greebles. Shape detection can't tell the difference
3. Widen it: the DOJ can add exceptions. Ask for cosplay, theater, schools, airsoft and replica builders

slides.heading: Prop Builders: What to Ask For
bullets: 4. Comment when the DOJ writes rules: ask for an appeal button, offline use, and detection of working gun parts instead of shapes
5. Build a false-positive library: everyday files the scanners wrongly flag, like hose triggers and tubes
Don't stretch the exemption to dodge the law. It says "exclusively" and "entertainment industry"

topics.title: Toolchanger Race: Creality K3 Dates, Bambu's FCC Parade
topics.description: K3 pre-orders open mid-October under $900, and Bambu's FCC filings keep coming

slides.heading: Creality K3: Missed Q3, Pre-Orders Mid-October
slides.body: Creality's Q3 target came and went. Its September 30 FAQ gives the new plan.
bullets: Pre-orders open mid-October. Price "expected to launch below $900"
Klipper-based firmware, released in phases. Root access out of the box
First hands-on: Creality brought the K3 to 3DPrintopia last weekend
No ship date yet

slides.heading: Bambu's FCC Parade
slides.body: Still no announcement, but the regulatory filings keep piling up.
bullets: S1 3D scanner: filed September 22, 60 W, likely handheld. Bambu's first scanner
AMS 3H and AMS 3P: new filament systems in the same filings
Also filed in September: H3C, P3C and an X2D Pro
Everything here comes from filings. Prices and dates floating around are guesses

slides.heading: The Chube Compact Is Here
slides.body: About a year after pre-orders opened, Luke's Laboratory is shipping. Mitsu Makes got one: "It only took a whole year..."

slides.heading: Chube Compact: What You're Getting
bullets: Shipped: about 25% of pre-orders by September 22, past 36% as of today
$139.99 pre-order price, now $170. New orders ship after all pre-orders
33 mm melt zone, 50 g, 80 W heater, PT1000 included

bullets: $199.99. Up to 400 °C, 110 °C above the stock hotend

topics.title: Robotics Corner: WAAM, Metal Printing with a Robot Welder
topics.description: ADAXIS and Fronius team up on wire-arc additive manufacturing

slides.heading: Robotics Corner: Printing Metal with a Welder
slides.body: ADAXIS (AdaOne robot-printing software) and Fronius (welding) teamed up on WAAM: wire-arc additive manufacturing.

slides.heading: WAAM in Plain English
bullets: A robot arm and a welding arc melt ordinary welding wire, bead by bead. Think a giant FDM printer for metal
Fast and huge: roughly 2–8 kg per hour, with parts several meters long
Steel, stainless, aluminum, bronze, Inconel, titanium. The catch: ridged parts that need heat treatment and machining
This collab: Fronius's CMT Additive PRO welding settings, driven by ADAXIS's toolpath and simulation software
Scale check (Sep 21): ORNL printed a nearly 2-ton steel mold for Boeing in 8 weeks

topics.title: Quick Tip of the Week
topics.description: Glow-in-the-dark Halloween prints: start with a hardened nozzle

slides.heading: Quick Tip: Glow Filament Eats Brass Nozzles
slides.body: It's Halloween printing season. Swap to a hardened steel nozzle before you load glow filament.
bullets: Glow comes from strontium aluminate, a very hard powder. Prusa calls its glow PETG "the most abrasive material we've ever made"
Use hardened steel (a 0.6 mm helps). Heavy use also wears PTFE tubes and extruder gears
Dry it first. Then charge with UV or daylight: most of the glow comes in the first 1.5 hours
